verdicts.object: The run-to-run spread of accuracy and output strings of five served LLMs at temperature zero on eight fixed BBH/MMLU task subsets across ten identical runs, reported as a measurement of instability.
verdicts.quote: Here we look at an additional source of uncertainty, performance variance from the same trained model on the same inputs when temperature=0.
verdicts.reason: OCCUPIES: the same-weights in-situ spread is measured but never used as a floor to grade a comparison of the model with an earlier or differently-served self (the local-GPU Llama-3-8B run is an ungraded aside), no interval is put on any comparison, and the object is accuracy and output strings rather than log-probabilities.
verdicts.nearer_reason: Same distance as Thinking Machines 2025: both measure a same-weights spread of served completions and neither grades a comparison against it; Atil et al. predate it (Aug 2024) and add only an ungraded local-GPU-versus-API contrast for Llama-3-8B.
verdicts.neighbour_phrase: Atil et al. measure output and accuracy spread across ten temperature-zero runs of five served LLMs

bearing_quotes: We investigate non-determinism in five LLMs configured to be deterministic when applied to eight common tasks in across 10 runs, in both zero-shot and few-shot settings.
We set the temperature at 0, top-p at 1, and fix the seed. We use the same compute infrastructure, inputs, and configurations.
Total agreement rate@N (TAR@N): the percentage of test set questions across N runs where generated answers are all identical, regardless of whether the answer was correct.
Note that we do not report standard deviations of means because the distributions across runs for a given condition are not normally distributed (see below).
Accuracy over 20 identical runs on college math, temperature=0, top-p=1. Median in blue, mean in black with dashed 5% and 95% quantiles.

In order to support this line of reasoning, we ran Llama3-8b on our local GPUs without any optimizations, yielding deterministic results. This indicates that the models and GPUs themselves are not the only source of non-determinism.

Additionally, we fine-tuned gpt-3.5 using two-fold cross validation. Although, the results indicate that fine-tuning helps reduce instability, we hypothesize that a fine tuned model cannot be shared across users and as such our tasks were the only ones being run.
We encourage reporting maximum-minimum scores across runs to have a more robust comparison of models.
leads: Yifan Song, Guoyin Wang, Sujian Li, and Bill Yuchen Lin. The good, the bad, and the greedy: Evaluation of LLMs should not ignore non-determinism. arXiv preprint arXiv:2407.10457, 2024.

Shuyin Ouyang, Jie M. Zhang, Mark Harman, and Meng Wang. An empirical study of the non-determinism of ChatGPT in code generation. ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology, 34(2), January 2025.
sources.notes: Atil et al. measure the floor and nothing else: ten temperature-zero runs per condition on the same API, reported as TAR@10 and max-min accuracy spread with quantiles but no standard deviations and no interval on any comparison; the item set is fixed (eight task subsets, 100-282 items each) but not hashed. The local-GPU Llama-3-8B run and the gpt-3.5 fine-tune are asides in the Discussion, not graded comparisons; the two leads are the same nondeterminism-measurement class, not nearer.

verdicts.object: Identification of which of 42 LLM versions an LLM-integrated application is serving, from generated-text responses to eight fixed crafted queries fed to a trained classifier or a signature database.
verdicts.quote: We model an adversary A whose objective is to determine the exact version vi of the LLM deployed in remote application B with the minimal number of queries to O. We refer to this adversarial goal as “LLM fingerprinting”.
verdicts.reason: OCCUPIES: the practice fingerprints a served model to identify which version it is (provenance); there is no comparison of a model with its own earlier or differently-served self, no same-weights floor, and no interval on such a comparison, the only standard deviations being over ten training runs of the classifier; the object is generated text, not log-probabilities.
verdicts.nearer_reason: Provenance identification is a different object from both pass-2 neighbours; Appendix C's cosine distances between fine-tuned derivatives and their base model are derivative detection with no floor.
verdicts.neighbour_phrase: Pasquini et al. identify which LLM version an application serves across 42 versions from eight fixed queries

bearing_quotes: LLMmap employs an active fingerprinting approach, sending carefully crafted queries to the application and analyzing the responses to identify the specific LLM version in use.
(2) Intra-model Consistency: A robust query should produce stable outputs even when the LLM is subjected to different prompting configurations or randomness.
However, it assumes access to the logits output generated by the LLM being tested, rather than the actual generated text.
After this optimization process, we finalized a query strategy composed of 8 highly effective queries, which are listed in Table G.2.
Accuracies and standard deviation computed on 10 models’ training runs.
Given those 5 models, we use the open-set LLMmap to derive a fingerprint signature for each variant and compare their vector signature with the vector signature of the base model.
However, we observed that the scale of the minimum distance often depended on the specific LLM under consideration, making it highly variable taken alone.
Fingerprinting a model q is then performed by finding the vector signature in the database DB that is closest to f(q).
leads: Mark Russinovich and Ahmed Salem. Hey, that’s my model! introducing chain & hash, an llm fingerprinting technique. arXiv preprint arXiv:2407.10887, 2024.
sources.notes: A provenance tool for red teams: eight fixed text probes (banner grabbing, alignment refusals, malformed input, prompt-injection triggers) and an 8M-parameter classifier or cosine-matched signature database; the ±figures in Table 2 are over ten training runs of the classifier, and Appendix E's unseen-model detector thresholds distances between different models, not a same-weights spread. Yang & Wu (their [47], logit-based) is already L04 on the closed list; the Russinovich & Salem lead hashes responses to predefined queries but for ownership, so it is a mechanism echo, not a nearer object.

verdicts.object: Attribution of a black-box LLM to its model family (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Phi) by an Auditor LLM that evolves prompts across trials and a Detective LLM that picks the two same-source models out of a lineup.
verdicts.quote: The Detective is informed that two of the models in the set are from the same "source" (either identical models or from the same model family). Its task is to identify these two models based on similarities in their outputs.
verdicts.reason: OCCUPIES: the practice attributes a model to a family from a lineup using prompts that change every trial; missing are a fixed item set, a same-weights floor, an interval on any comparison and a log-probability object, and the cohorts holding two instances of the same model are a lineup identification, not a graded self-comparison.
verdicts.nearer_reason: Family attribution with an evolving prompt set is farther from C4a than either pass-2 neighbour; nothing is graded against a same-weights spread.
verdicts.neighbour_phrase: Iourovitski et al. identify an LLM's family across a lineup using LLM-generated evolving prompts

bearing_quotes: In this work, we introduce a novel black-box approach for fingerprinting LLMs, achieving an impressive 72% accuracy in identifying the correct family of models (Such as Llama, Mistral, Gemma, etc) among a lineup of LLMs.
This is done while assuming that all LLM models will be treated as black boxes, with their internal workings and training data remaining unknown.
By iteratively refining prompts through in-context learning, our system uncovers subtle distinctions between model outputs, providing a powerful tool for LLM analysis and verification.
Due to the stochastic nature of Language models generating content, there will naturally be a variability in accuracy as showcased.
Unlike the auditor which is provided the outputs of previous turns, the detective/evaluator is only provided the model outputs from the current turn.

We use a max of 10 trials and this is mostly limited by the Auditors Context Length, additional context length could allow for more trials, but current findings indicate if a pattern can be found, its usually within the first three to five iterations.
2 instances of Llama-8B were marked as similar by the auditor across two trials
2 instances of Phi-2-2.7B were trialed without success by auditor across five trials
sources.notes: Short workshop-style paper; the only quantitative result is family-detection accuracy shown as violin plots (Figure 2) with no numbers in the text beyond the 72% headline, and no floor, interval or fixed item set anywhere. Some cohorts pair two instances of identical weights, which is the closest it comes to a model-with-itself object, but the Detective only has to find the pair in a lineup.

verdicts.object: Cryptographic verification, by an interactive proof, that an untrusted cloud executed a known small neural network (an arithmetic circuit with quadratic activations) exactly on a batch of client inputs.
verdicts.quote: Note that the SafetyNets is not intended to and cannot catch any inherent mis-classiﬁcations due to the model itself, only those that result from incorrect computations of the model by the server.
verdicts.reason: OCCUPIES: the practice verifies inference cryptographically for a network known to both parties; there is no behavioural comparison of a served model with its earlier or differently-served self, no fixed hashed item set, no same-weights floor, and the only bound is the proof's soundness error, not an interval on a comparison.
verdicts.nearer_reason: Exact-execution proofs for a known 2017-era DNN are a different object from both pass-2 neighbours and from any behavioural fingerprint.
verdicts.neighbour_phrase: Ghodsi et al. verify a cloud's exact execution of a known network across batches via interactive proofs

bearing_quotes: We propose SafetyNets, a framework that enables an untrusted server (the cloud) to provide a client with a short mathematical proof of the correctness of inference tasks that they perform on behalf of the client.
A lazy cloud might use a simpler but less accurate model, for instance, a single-layer instead of a multi-layer neural network, to reduce its computational costs.
In our setting, f(.) is a trained multi-layer neural network that is known to both the veriﬁer and prover, and y is the neural network’s classiﬁcation output for each image in the batch.
SafetyNets applies to a certain class of neural networks that can be represented as arithmetic circuits that perform computations over ﬁnite ﬁelds (i.e., integers modulo a large prime p).
Instead, in SafetyNets, the prover computes and sends zL−1 (the input of the ﬁnal activation layer) as a result to the veriﬁer.

SafetyNets detects any incorrect computations of the neural network by the untrusted server with high probability, while achieving state-of-the-art accuracy on the MNIST digit recognition (99.4%) and TIMIT speech recognition tasks (75.22%).
If the server incorrectly computes the output corresponding to any input in a batch, the veriﬁer rejects the entire batch of computations.
Audits based on the server’s execution time [14] require precise knowledge of the server’s hardware conﬁguration and assume, for instance, that the server is not over-clocked.
sources.notes: GKR/Thaler sum-check proofs over a finite field for MNIST and TIMIT networks; the verified quantity is the pre-softmax layer input z_{L-1}, checked for exact equality rather than used as a behavioural statistic, and the sole bound is a soundness error below 2^-30 on the proof. The paper says outright it cannot catch the model's own misclassifications, so it has no behavioural object at all; the extracted text carries ﬁ ligatures, preserved in the quotes above.
